title: Docs, Examples & User Onboarding
scope: Evaluate documentation quality, example scripts, scripts/, and user guidance.

doc_sites.format: VitePress (Vue-based static site generator) with custom theme
doc_sites.custom_theme_dir: docs/.vitepress/theme/ (EvolutionBanner.vue, index.ts, style.css — EvolutionBanner shows a banner redirecting users to the newer Kimi Code project)
doc_sites.i18n: Two locales: English (/en/) and Simplified Chinese (/zh/) with mirrored directory paths and filenames. docs/index.md auto-redirects to /en/ or /zh/ based on navigator.language.

plugins.name: vitepress-plugin-mermaid
plugins.purpose: Render Mermaid diagrams in markdown (flowcharts, etc.)

plugins.name: vitepress-plugin-llms
plugins.purpose: Generate llms.txt / llms-full.txt for LLM consumption; bundled in vite config

structure.Guides: getting-started, use-cases, interaction, sessions, ides, integrations
structure.Customization: mcp, plugins, hooks, skills, agents, print-mode, wire-mode
structure.Reference: kimi-command, kimi-info, kimi-acp, kimi-mcp, kimi-term, kimi-vis, kimi-web, slash-commands, keyboard
structure.FAQ: faq (single page, categorized by topic: setup/auth, interaction, ACP, MCP, print/wire, updates)

doc_sites.source_of_truth: Chinese docs (docs/zh/) are the source of truth for content; English changelog (docs/en/release-notes/changelog.md) is auto-generated from root CHANGELOG.md via docs/scripts/sync-changelog.mjs. Other English pages may be auto-translated by AI agents.

docs_scripts.docs/scripts/sync-changelog.mjs: Node script that converts root CHANGELOG.md (## [x.y] - YYYY-MM-DD format) into docs/en/release-notes/changelog.md (## x.y (YYYY-MM-DD) format), stripping HTML comments and subsection headers. Runs before vitepress dev/build via npm scripts.
docs_scripts.docs/package.json: Private npm package with scripts: sync (run changelog sync), dev (sync + vitepress dev), build (sync + vitepress build), preview.

doc_sites.content_pattern: Pages are scaffolds with heading outlines + 'Reference Code' blocks listing source files to reference. Authoring workflow: expand bullets into prose, keep section ordering, keep reference-code blocks aligned. Naming: kebab-case filenames mirrored across locales. See docs/AGENTS.md for full style guide.
doc_sites.other_formats: No Markdown/MDX/RST beyond VitePress-flavored Markdown (.md). No separate MDX or RST sites. README-driven content is minimal (README.md in repo root links to docs site). llms.txt is auto-generated by the llms plugin.
doc_sites.build: Docs built from docs/ directory: npm install; npm run dev; npm run build; output to docs/.vitepress/dist
doc_sites.github_pages: Deployed via .github/workflows/docs-pages.yml triggered on push to main

examples.location: examples/ (7 subdirectories, each with README.md + main.py)
examples.purpose_summary: Self-contained runnable demos showing how to embed, extend, or invoke Kimi Code CLI programmatically from Python.

list.name: custom-echo-soul
list.purpose: Demonstrates writing a custom Soul (agent loop) implementation from scratch that echoes user input back. Implements the minimal Soul protocol (name, model_name, model_capabilities, status, available_slash_commands, run) and plugs it into the Shell UI.
list.usage: cd examples/custom-echo-soul; uv sync --reinstall; uv run main.py

list.name: custom-kimi-soul
list.purpose: Demonstrates extending the built-in KimiSoul class to customize agent loop behavior (overrides name property, run method) while reusing the standard tool chain, then wrapping with the Shell UI.
list.usage: cd examples/custom-kimi-soul; uv sync --reinstall; uv run main.py

list.name: custom-tools
list.purpose: Demonstrates writing a custom tool (my_tools/ls.py: Ls class extending CallableTool2) and registering it in an agent YAML spec (myagent.yaml) alongside built-in tools, then running in print mode.
list.usage: cd examples/custom-tools; uv sync --reinstall; uv run main.py

list.name: kimi-cli-stream-json
list.purpose: Demonstrates running Kimi CLI as a subprocess in non-interactive print mode with --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json, sending JSONL messages over stdin and reading JSONL responses over stdout.

list.name: kimi-cli-wire-messages
list.purpose: Demonstrates using KimiCLI.create() + instance.run() programmatically with merge_wire_messages=True to consume raw Wire message objects directly from Python (lower-level than stream-json, uses kaos.kimi_cli.app and kimi_cli.session APIs).
list.usage: cd examples/kimi-cli-wire-messages; uv sync --reinstall; uv run main.py

list.name: kimi-psql
list.purpose: AI-assisted PostgreSQL interactive terminal. Combines an AI mode (natural-language to SQL via a custom ExecuteSql tool using psycopg in read-only transactions) with a full interactive psql mode (PTY-based), switchable via Ctrl-X. Demonstrates building a specialized TUI app on top of kimi-cli's soul/ui components.
list.usage: cd examples/kimi-psql; uv sync --reinstall; uv run main.py --conninfo 'postgresql://user:pass@host/db'

list.name: sample-plugin
list.purpose: Demonstrates the plugin/skills system: a plugin.json manifest declaring two external tools (py_greet in Python, ts_calc in TypeScript via npx tsx) with JSON Schema parameters, plus a SKILL.md frontmatter file. Shows language-agnostic tool definitions.
list.usage: cd examples/sample-plugin; uv run python scripts/greet.py (for Python tool); npx tsx scripts/calc.ts (for TS tool)

examples.common_pattern: All Python examples follow: cd <example-dir>; uv sync --reinstall; uv run main.py. They import from kimi_cli (app, session, soul, ui, wire, config, llm, auth) and kosong (tooling primitives). Each example is a uv project with its own pyproject.toml.

scripts.purpose_summary: Build, release, maintenance, and debugging utilities invoked via uv run; wired into the Makefile and CI workflows.

list.name: install.sh
list.purpose: Linux/macOS installation entry point. Installs uv (via curl or wget from astral.sh), then runs 'uv tool install --python 3.13 kimi-cli'.

list.name: install.ps1
list.purpose: Windows PowerShell equivalent of install.sh. Installs uv, updates PATH, then runs 'uv tool install --python 3.13 kimi-cli'.

list.name: build_web.py
list.purpose: Builds the web UI (from web/) using npm + Vite, verifies version tag in build output, then copies dist to src/kimi_cli/web/static. Supports strict version checking via KIMI_WEB_STRICT_VERSION/KIMI_WEB_EXPECT_VERSION.
list.invoked_by: make build-web (called by build-kimi-cli / build-bin / build-bin-onedir)

list.name: build_vis.py
list.purpose: Builds the vis UI (from vis/) using npm + Vite, checks Node.js version (requires ^20.19.0 or >=22.12.0 for Vite 7), then copies dist to src/kimi_cli/vis/static.

list.name: inject_build_sha.py
list.purpose: Injects git commit SHA (+ normalized remote origin URL) into src/kimi_cli/_build_info.py for telemetry provenance. Called before wheel builds and PyInstaller binary builds. Reads KIMI_BUILD_SHA env var or git rev-parse HEAD.

list.name: check_version_tag.py
list.purpose: Validates that a git release tag matches the version in a package's pyproject.toml. Enforces x.y.z semver format. Used by all release workflows (kimi-cli, kosong, pykaos, kimi-sdk).

list.name: check_kimi_dependency_versions.py
list.purpose: Validates that kimi-cli's root pyproject.toml has pinned (==) dependency versions matching the actual versions in packages/kosong and packages/kaos (pykaos). Ensures workspace alignment.

list.name: cleanup_tmp_sessions.py
list.purpose: Cleans up kimi sessions whose workdir is under a temporary directory. Two phases: (1) removes kimi.json entries + session dirs for tmp paths, (2) removes orphan session directories. Default is dry-run; --apply actually deletes. Detects /tmp, /private/tmp, /var/folders, /private/var/folders prefixes.

list.name: telemetry_debug_server.py
list.purpose: Tiny local HTTP server (http.server) on 127.0.0.1:8765/v1/event for inspecting outbound telemetry events. Prints matched events as pretty-printed JSON. Configurable via EVENT_FILTER variable.

klips.meaning: Kimi CLI Improvement Proposal — RFC-style lightweight design documents (YAML frontmatter: Author, Updated, Status) that record architectural decisions, feature designs, and rationale for kimi-cli.
klips.purpose: Capture 'essence changes' to data structures/protocols/interfaces before implementation, following a design-first workflow where agents propose requirements, programmers think about essential changes, and both co-author the KLIP. Serves as the living spec that code is generated from. Each KLIP includes: background/current-state, goals, non-goals, design overview, implementation plan, compatibility/boundary analysis, test plan, and references to key source files.

onboarding.target_user: New developer/user installing Kimi Code CLI for the first time

steps.detail: Python 3.12-3.14 (Python 3.13 recommended). uv package manager recommended.

Option A (recommended): curl -LsSf https://code.kimi.com/install.sh | bash (Linux/macOS) or Invoke-RestMethod https://code.kimi.com/install.ps1 | Invoke-Expression (Windows). The install script installs uv then runs 'uv tool install --python 3.13 kimi-cli'. Option B: uv tool install --python 3.13 kimi-cli (if uv already installed).
cd your-project; kimi — starts the interactive shell UI in agent mode

On first launch, run /login to select a platform. Kimi Code platform uses OAuth (browser-based, automatically opens verification URL). Other platforms require a manual API key. /setup is the alternative for manual API key configuration (selects platform -> inputs API key -> fetches models -> writes config). Settings are saved to ~/.kimi/config.toml and auto-reloaded.

Run /help to view all slash commands (categorized: help/info, config/debug, session management, others). Run /init to auto-generate an AGENTS.md file for the current project so the AI understands project structure and conventions.

onboarding.data_locations: ~/.kimi/ holds config.toml, kimi.json (metadata), mcp.json (MCP servers), sessions/ (context.jsonl + wire.jsonl per session), user-history/, logs/kimi.log. Skills discovered from builtin, ~/.config/agents/skills/, ~/.kimi/skills/, ~/.claude/skills/ (user level), and .agents/skills/ (project level).
onboarding.usage_modes: kimi (interactive shell UI with Typer CLI), kimi web (browser-based UI on localhost), kimi acp (ACP server for IDE integration with Zed/JetBrains).
onboarding.key_flags: --work-dir (set working directory), --continue/--session (resume sessions), --print (non-interactive), --input-format/--output-format (stream-json/plain/json), --agent-file (custom agent spec), --yolo (auto-approve), --thinking/--no-thinking, --mcp-config-file/--mcp-config (ad-hoc MCP), --skills-dir (override skill discovery).
onboarding.config_overrides: Environment variables KIMI_BASE_URL, KIMI_API_KEY, KIMI_MODEL_NAME, KIMI_MODEL_MAX_CONTEXT_SIZE, KIMI_MODEL_CAPABILITIES, KIMI_MODEL_TEMPERATURE, KIMI_MODEL_TOP_P, KIMI_MODEL_MAX_TOKENS, KIMI_CLI_NO_AUTO_UPDATE. Also OpenAI-compatible: OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY.
onboarding.upgrade_uninstall: Upgrade: uv tool upgrade kimi-cli --no-cache. Uninstall: uv tool uninstall kimi-cli.
onboarding.dev_setup: For contributors: git clone https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-cli.git; cd kimi-cli; make prepare (syncs all workspace deps + installs prek hooks). Then: uv run kimi (run CLI), make format, make check, make test, make build.

findings.proposal: ai-factory should adopt the VitePress + i18n + scaffold-driven docs pattern proven by kimi-cli: host docs in docs/ as VitePress markdown with kebab-case mirrored EN/ZH slugs, a CI hook that auto-syncs the changelog (and ideally config-schema docs) from source-of-truth files, and a lightweight YAML frontmatter convention (status, assigned_agent, dependencies, scope, folders) so docs and research notes live alongside code. Onboarding should follow kimi-cli's install -> verify -> first-run -> /login -> /help -> /init flow, delivered via an executable install script (curl|bash) that bootstraps uv then uv-installs the package, with a /login-style config wizard (OAuth or API-key) backed by a persistent default config location (~/.kimi/config.toml equivalent) and environment-variable overrides (e.g. KIMI_API_KEY equivalent) so that new users can go from zero to their first agent turn in three commands: install, cd project, run.
